findings.suggested_fix: Build the ISR function with a distinct entrypoint or build-time flag and accept `x_astro_path` only there; retain the existing secret-gated behavior in `_render`.
findings.title: Do not trust the ISR header in the shared render handler
findings.why_it_matters: A request to the ordinary render function can select a different Astro route by supplying both `x-vercel-isr: 1` and `x_astro_path`, defeating the existing path-override protection and potentially bypassing path-specific Vercel routing or access controls. The same entrypoint is built for both `_render` and `_isr`, so the header alone does not establish which function received the request. Restrict the override to a separately configured ISR entrypoint or another trusted signal that cannot be supplied by the caller.

findings.suggested_fix: Extend the adapter tests to invoke the built _isr function with x-vercel-isr: 1 and x_astro_path and assert the requested page is rendered; also test the same header and query parameter against _render and assert that an untrusted request cannot change its route.
findings.title: Exercise ISR path recovery through the built function
findings.why_it_matters: The intended ISR fix can regress while the existing ISR suite still passes: it checks generated configuration and routes, but never invokes the built ISR function or verifies the matched page. The existing path override security tests also do not exercise a request carrying the newly trusted header, so they do not catch unintended overrides on the regular render function. Covering both requests through the generated function would verify restoration and preserve the existing security contract.

findings.title: ISR requests expose the internal path as a query parameter
findings.why_it_matters: Pages and middleware see x_astro_path in Astro.url and Request.url even when the visitor supplied no query string. Applications that branch on query presence, preserve a return URL, or generate canonical URLs consequently produce incorrect output for ISR requests.

residual_risks: The repository does not establish whether Vercel strips or replaces client-provided x-vercel-isr headers before invoking a function; deployment-level exploitability depends on that behavior.

The handler accepts x_astro_path as a route override whenever x-vercel-isr is 1, including on the _render function. Whether an external client can cause this condition depends on Vercel's handling of the header and rewrite query parameters, which cannot be verified from this checkout. If clients can supply both, path-based platform protections or ISR exclusions could be bypassed.
Vercel platform behavior, including whether its ISR header is always present and how it encodes substituted paths, could not be verified in this environment.
testing_gaps: The existing path-override security tests do not exercise an untrusted x-vercel-isr header together with x_astro_path; a deployed Vercel test is needed to establish whether that combination reaches the handler.
